source_index.equipment:K-3401:engineer_comment: Single train, no spare, no workaround. If it trips the platform goes to recycle and production is cut within the hour. Vibration is trended daily and anything unusual gets a rotating equipment specialist the same day.
source_index.equipment:LB-4102:engineer_comment: Certified survival craft under class survey. Any defect that could prevent launch reduces the total evacuation capacity of the installation, which is compared against the POB count. That comparison is not negotiable.
source_index.equipment:P-3305:engineer_comment: Fussy little unit, diaphragm failures every few months. Losing it does not stop production so it gets deprioritised, but inhibitor starvation means the downstream carbon steel starts corroding within weeks. The consequence lands six months later on someone else's desk.
source_index.equipment:PL-1002:engineer_comment: Live hydrocarbon line at full wellhead pressure. Corrosion under insulation is the known threat here and it is invisible until the cladding comes off.
source_index.equipment:PL-1002:service_description: 6 inch production flowline - manifold to V-1201
source_index.equipment:PSV-1310:engineer_comment: Certified relief device on a two year pop test cycle. Any evidence of passing or weeping is treated as an impairment of a protection layer, not as a maintenance nuisance. There is a regulatory clock on impaired relief devices.
source_index.equipment:PSV-3420:engineer_comment: Same regime as PSV-1310. Recently recertified and behaving itself.
source_index.equipment:SC-1001:engineer_comment: Fabric maintenance here is chronically behind, so coating breakdown reports are frequent and mostly cosmetic. Section loss at a node or a cracked weld at a primary connection is a completely different severity and should never be batched with the coating backlog.
source_index.equipment:V-1201:engineer_comment: Thick walled and historically trouble free, but it is the pressure boundary for the entire first stage. Any indication of wall loss, cracking or weeping goes to the integrity engineer regardless of how small it looks.
source_index.equipment:V-1305:engineer_comment: Only used during well testing. Can be isolated and bypassed indefinitely with no production impact. Findings here can usually wait for the next planned shutdown.
source_index.equipment:V-2450:engineer_comment: Protects the turbines from liquid carryover. Not glamorous, but a liquid slug into a gas turbine is an expensive afternoon.
source_index.finding:F-1001:finding_description: Overall vibration on the non-drive end bearing has climbed from 2.1 mm/s to 4.6 mm/s over the last six weeks. Spectrum shows a growing 1x component with some sidebands. Not at alarm yet but the trend is clearly upward and it has not plateaued.
source_index.finding:F-1003:finding_description: Pump failed to start on the first attempt during the weekly test. Started on the second attempt after about eight seconds of cranking. Starting batteries measured 22.8 V at rest which is on the low side. Ran normally once started and achieved rated discharge pressure.
source_index.finding:F-1004:finding_description: Removed cladding at three inspection windows on the 6 inch flowline. At window 2 near the low point drain the insulation was saturated and there is heavy scaling on the pipe surface. UT readings at that location give 6.2 mm against a nominal 11.1 mm and a minimum allowable of 7.4 mm. Adjacent windows are within tolerance.
source_index.finding:F-1005:finding_description: Detector head did not respond to 50 percent LEL test gas. Repeated with a second cylinder, still no response. Head appears clean, no obvious damage to the optics. The other two heads in the same voted group responded correctly.
source_index.finding:F-1006:finding_description: Annual lifting appliance survey. Main hoist wire rope shows 6 broken wires within one lay length in the section that spools onto the drum at maximum boom radius. Discard criterion for this rope construction is 10 broken wires per lay length. Rope lubrication is poor along the same section. Hook, sheaves and structure all satisfactory.
source_index.finding:F-1007:finding_description: Corrosion inhibitor pump has tripped again on low discharge pressure. This is the third time this month. Suspect the diaphragm. Injection to the wellhead manifold has been intermittent for around ten days according to the injection log.
source_index.finding:F-1008:finding_description: Crack indication found at the toe of the weld connecting a primary brace to the cellar deck node at grid B4. Confirmed by MPI, length approximately 45 mm. This is a primary structural connection. Surrounding coating is intact so this is not a general fabric issue.
source_index.finding:F-1009:finding_description: General coating breakdown across the underside of the cellar deck plating between grids C2 and C5. Rust staining and flaking primer over a large area. This has been reported before and is on the fabric maintenance backlog.
source_index.finding:F-1010:finding_description: Temporary refuge pressurisation test carried out. Measured differential pressure across the accommodation envelope was 27 Pa against a required minimum of 50 Pa. Fan is running at rated speed. Suspect either a damper not fully closing or degraded door seals somewhere in the envelope.
source_index.finding:F-1012:finding_description: Hydraulic release mechanism on the freefall lifeboat did not operate cleanly during the annual survey. Required significantly more force than specification and the movement was notchy. Surveyor has withheld the certificate pending overhaul of the release gear. Lifeboat is currently declared unavailable.
source_index.finding:F-1016:finding_description: Certification tag on the compressor discharge PSV is illegible, the label has corroded. Checked the register and the valve was recertified in March 2025 so it is in date. Physical condition of the valve looks fine.
source_index.finding:F-1017:finding_description: Firewater pump A started first time and ran up correctly but discharge pressure stabilised at 9.2 barg against a design of 11 barg. Flow was not measured. Engine parameters all normal. Suspect either pump internal wear or a partly closed valve somewhere in the test line.
source_index.finding:F-1019:finding_description: Lagging on the second stage discharge line has come loose and a section of cladding is flapping in the wind. No process concern but it will end up as a dropped object if left.
source_index.knowledge:item-42cdf410e42da4981ff0812d1:
## Output expectations

Maintenance planning needs two lines: what is wrong, on what, and why it matters — readable without
opening the inspection record, and not a restatement of the original finding text. Where the
assessment is uncertain, that should be stated rather than resolved by picking a mid-range score.

Recurring causes of loss of confidence in a triage output, in order:

1. Confidently incorrect scores on safety critical equipment.
2. Summaries that omit a detail that changes the decision — a measurement, a repeat occurrence, the
   fact that the standby was already unavailable.
3. The same finding scored differently on different days.
4. Uniform mid-range scores across all findings.
source_index.knowledge:item-54adfcd342912676dbeb55a8e:
## Two recurring errors

**Voted arrangements.** One detector head out of a 2oo3 group is a degradation, not a defeat. The
arrangement still functions, so impact is moderate rather than extreme. It is time-limited, because
the group has lost its margin and the next failure defeats it.

**Redundancy is a claim, not a fact.** Check whether the redundant partner is healthy before crediting
it. If findings exist against both legs of a redundant pair in the same batch, the pair is not
redundant. Assessing each finding in isolation misses this.
source_index.knowledge:item-73e154e8c17d78a3f93dfe3d3:
## Registry scores

`reliability_score` is 10 = highly reliable, 1 = frequent failures. It runs in the opposite direction
to likelihood. New starters routinely invert it. `criticality_score` runs in the expected direction,
10 = most critical.

Neither is sufficient on its own. Criticality is a starting point for impact, reliability a starting
point for likelihood; the finding text moves both. A reliable item with a crack in it is still
cracked.
source_index.knowledge:item-755a159e23ccfabc4caf1e2fa:
## What moves likelihood

Up: a trend that is still moving; a repeat of a failure that has already occurred this period; an
active, unmitigated mechanism (corrosion under wet insulation is progressing now); detection by a
method that only catches late-stage damage — a finding detected by ear or smell is further advanced
than one detected by UT.

Down: design margin; a measurement inside its acceptance criterion; an item that is out of service
and not required to be in service.
source_index.knowledge:item-9e493f0f702c0a96796002139:
## The two questions

**Likelihood** concerns the item itself: given what the inspection found, how likely is it to stop
performing its function in the near term. A hairline coating blister on a thick-walled vessel is low
likelihood even on a critical vessel. A bearing with a vibration trend that has not plateaued is high
likelihood even on a spare pump.

**Impact** concerns what happens if it does fail. This depends mainly on what the equipment does and
what sits behind it, not on the wording of the finding.

The common error is scoring by how severe the description sounds.
source_index.knowledge:item-c0781817a1f4c0adcd4f0cb6e:
# Integrity and Reliability Notes — Bravo Platform

Handover notes from the outgoing Integrity Engineer. Unedited. This is the only written record of how
findings are currently triaged.
source_index.knowledge:item-d7ced767260f196407f7f1b20:
## Urgency

Not an average of likelihood and impact, and not the maximum, though the maximum is closer. A
low-likelihood, high-impact finding on an SCE still requires attention this week. A near-certain
failure of something inconsequential can wait for the next shutdown. Urgency expresses how soon a
human must act.

- 9–10: today
- 7–8: this week
- 5–6: this month
- 3–4: next planned shutdown
- 1–2: backlog

Two conditions override the derived value. Anything that leaves a protection layer impaired without a
recorded deviation is immediate, because the installation is out of compliance from the point the
impairment is known. The same applies to anything that reduces evacuation capacity below the POB
count.
source_index.knowledge:item-eac29968ebd33c833e8961572:
## What moves impact

Up: absence of redundancy; Safety Critical Elements, which exist because a major accident scenario
depends on them and are judged against that scenario rather than against repair cost; failures that
degrade a protection layer rather than causing direct loss; delayed or hidden consequences — loss of
corrosion inhibitor has no effect today and a substantial effect in eighteen months; escalation
potential.

Down: redundancy that is available and capable; items that can be bypassed without loss of function;
atmospheric, non-hydrocarbon, low-energy services; consequences limited to housekeeping or appearance.
